newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ship sinks, drowning 1,600 Australian cattle.
newsitem.headline: Ship sinks, drowning 1,600 Australian cattle.

text.p: About 1,600 head of Australian cattle drowned when a Philippines registered ship sank off Guam in a typhoon, an Australian livestock official said on Monday.
The Guernsey Express livestock carrier went down in huge seas early on Sunday, 40 nautical miles southwest of Guam, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC) said in a statement.
The 4,255 tonne ship sank at the peak of Typhoon Dale, which generated 300 kmh (237 mph) winds and 13 metre (45 foot) seas.
The 20-man crew spent six hours in a lifeboat before being rescued by the U.S. coastguard, the statement said.
The A$1.6 million (US$1.2 million) cattle shipment was bound for Osaka, Japan.
"It's a very unfortunate, a regrettable first," said AMLC spokesman Chris Rowley. The sinking was the first time a shipload of live Australian cattle had been lost.
In September, almost 70,000 Australian sheep perished in a burning ship which sunk off the Seychelles off eastern Africa.
Australia has lost two shiploads of live sheep in recent years, the first going down in 1980 off Australia's southern coast drowning all 41,000 sheep on board headed for Iran.
The Australian government said that despite the losses, the export of live sheep and cattle would continue.
"There'll be no stopping of the export trade," Robert Haynes, spokesman for Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson, told Reuters.

The cattle shipment formed part of a A$500 million live animal trade which saw 627,000 live cattle exported in 1995/96, with 750,000 head expected to be exported in 1996/97. Australia exported 5.54 million live sheep last year.

Most of Australia's live animal exports go to Indonesia and the Philippines, where animal processing costs are one-tenth those in Australia, but Japan has also developed into a lucrative destination. (A$1=US40.79)
